exploration.title: Pattern Palace
exploration.subject: Mathematics
exploration.summary: Rotate and reflect a motif, then test how regular polygons fit around a point.
exploration.question: Why do some repeated shapes leave a gap while others fit exactly?
exploration.explanation: A rotation turns a shape around a point. A reflection flips it across a line; both preserve lengths and angles. A full turn is 360°. Equal regular polygons can meet without a gap or overlap only when their corner angles fill that turn. Six equilateral triangles, four squares or three regular hexagons do so. This model checks one meeting point; a successful corner test alone is not a proof that any proposed pattern tiles an entire floor.

experiments.title: Turn or flip?
experiments.instruction: Inspect the uneven motif. Predict where its marked point will move after a quarter-turn, then rotate it 90°. Compare with reflecting the motif.
experiments.observe: Compare the position of the marked point. Explain why turning and making a mirror image are different transformations even though lengths stay the same.

experiments.title: Fill a full turn
experiments.instruction: Predict how many squares meet at a point without gaps. Test four, then try three regular pentagons and four regular pentagons.
experiments.observe: Four square corners fill 360°. Three pentagon corners leave 36°, while four overlap by 72°. Explain why adding another pentagon does not solve the gap.

exploration.misconception: A regular shape does not necessarily tile a flat surface by itself. Its corner angles must fit with neighboring tiles without gaps or overlaps.
